waterSolubility: Cd²⁺ highly soluble in acidic soils; ~1000 mg/L as CdCl₂
environmentalPersistence: Very high — does not degrade; persists in soil for decades

lowDose.description: Subclinical — mild oxidative stress detectable biochemically but no visible morphological symptoms. Some studies show marginal growth stimulation in hyperaccumulator species but not in Coleus.

highDose.description: Severe root necrosis, dark leaf spotting, strong chlorosis, wilting, near-complete growth arrest. Metal accumulation visible as dark deposits in root and stem tissue.

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Strong — root uptake inhibition starves shoot of water and nutrients
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Mild — not a primary Cd symptom
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Strong — water uptake severely impaired by root damage
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strong — Cd displaces Fe and Zn from chlorophyll synthesis pathway
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Strong — dark brown-black spotting on leaves and root tips; stem base darkening
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Mild anthocyanin increase as oxidative stress response
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Severely inhibited — primary site of Cd toxicity; root tips blacken
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Both affected; chlorosis appears first on older leaves, spotting on all

physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Decreased — both ABA-mediated and direct damage to guard cells
physiologyEffects.nutrientTransport: Strongly disrupted — Cd competes with Ca, Fe, Zn, Mn

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Strong — one of Cd's primary mechanisms of toxicity
molecularEffects.lipidPeroxidation: Strong — MDA accumulation is a key biomarker

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Strong — Cd is broadly toxic to soil microbiome
microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Strongly suppressed — PGPR highly sensitive to Cd
microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Mycorrhizal fungi disrupted; Cd-tolerant fungal species may increase

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: Minimal — Cd is not metabolized; phytoremediation possible only over very long timescales
temporalDynamics.sensitization: Accumulative — symptoms worsen continuously as Cd builds up in tissue

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → yellow (chlorosis) with dark brown-black spots; roots turn brown-black
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Upward from roots through vascular tissue
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Patchy dark spotting on leaves; uniform chlorosis background
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Dark amber glow — phytochelatin and MDA accumulation signature; roots show strongest signal
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Sparse, slow; high pathogen fraction; resistome particles increase
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: No recovery — damage is permanent and progressive

synergies.synergyNote: Heavy metal combinations are additive to synergistic — shared ROS mechanism and phytochelatin competition means combined exposure overwhelms detox capacity faster
synergies.antagonismNote: Phosphorus and calcium compete with Cd for uptake sites; adequate P and Ca in soil reduces Cd bioavailability

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Phosphate fertilizers, industrial smelting, battery manufacturing, cigarette smoke, contaminated irrigation water
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Not intentionally used — a contaminant in phosphate fertilizers
educationalContext.humanToxicity: High — IARC Group 1 carcinogen; causes kidney damage, Itai-itai disease (bone softening); accumulates in food crops
educationalContext.climateLink: Increased soil acidification from climate change increases Cd mobility and bioavailability
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily outdoor/soil; indoor via cigarette smoke
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Enters the food chain through crops grown in contaminated soil — rice and leafy vegetables are major vectors. Direct link between industrial pollution and food safety.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Soil contamination, food safety, industrial pollution legacy sites
